scope: Proposition 5.1 of the manuscript “A counterexample to integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison” (preprints/A-counterexample-to-integer-degree-harmonic-dimension-comparison-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 361 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c6adbdbf2331bf0f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 18. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the fixed spectral data above, there are a smooth function a : R → (0, 1] and an index jgeom such that, for every j0 ≥ jgeom, every sequence (hj)j≥j0 in K, used in the preceding scheme, defines a smooth complete metric on Rm+1 with nonnegative Ricci curvature: g = dr2 + r2 γ(log r), γ(t) = G(a(t), q(t), J(t)). The function a is identically 1 for t ≤ 2, decreases to a∗, and, for some µ > 0, satisfies b(t) := a′(t) a(t) = −µ(1 + t)−5/4 (t ≥ 4), log a(t) a∗ = 4µ(1 + t)−1/4 (t ≥ 4). (5.2) The metric is Euclidean near the origin, and its distance from the origin is exactly r. Its volume form is d volg = rm a(log r)m dr d volg0 . The function a and the starting index j0 can be chosen independently of the sequence of control parameters.
